questions.question: Under FOB (Free On Board) terms, when does the risk transfer from the seller to the buyer?
options: When the goods are loaded onto the vessel at the port of shipment
When the goods arrive at the destination port
When the seller delivers goods to the freight forwarder
When the buyer pays for the goods
questions.answer: When the goods are loaded onto the vessel at the port of shipment
questions.explanation: Under FOB Incoterms, risk transfers from seller to buyer once the goods are loaded on board the vessel nominated by the buyer at the named port of shipment.

questions.question: CIF stands for:
questions.explanation: CIF (Cost, Insurance and Freight) means the seller pays for the cost of goods, marine insurance, and freight to bring goods to the destination port. Risk transfers when goods are on board the vessel.

questions.question: Under EXW (Ex Works) terms, who is responsible for loading the goods at the seller's premises?
options: The buyer bears all costs and risks from the seller's premises
The seller loads the goods onto the buyer's truck
The freight forwarder handles all loading
questions.answer: The buyer bears all costs and risks from the seller's premises
questions.explanation: EXW represents minimum obligation for the seller. The buyer takes all responsibility from the seller's warehouse, including loading, export clearance, and all transport costs.

questions.question: A Bill of Lading (B/L) serves as:
options: A receipt, a contract of carriage, and a document of title
Only a receipt for goods shipped
questions.answer: A receipt, a contract of carriage, and a document of title
questions.explanation: A Bill of Lading has three key functions: (1) Evidence of contract of carriage between shipper and carrier, (2) Receipt for goods shipped, (3) Document of title allowing the holder to claim the goods.

questions.question: What is a Packing List used for in international trade?
options: To detail the contents, weight, and dimensions of each package in a shipment
To show the price of goods
questions.answer: To detail the contents, weight, and dimensions of each package in a shipment
questions.explanation: A Packing List provides detailed information about the shipment including: number of packages, description of goods, net/gross weight, and dimensions. It assists customs authorities and the consignee to verify the shipment.

questions.question: What is the difference between FCL and LCL shipping?
options: FCL is a full container load, LCL shares space with other shippers
FCL is faster, LCL is slower
FCL is for air freight, LCL is for sea freight
FCL is cheaper, LCL is more expensive per unit
questions.answer: FCL is a full container load, LCL shares space with other shippers
questions.explanation: FCL (Full Container Load) means one shipper uses the entire container. LCL (Less than Container Load) means multiple shippers share one container, consolidated by a freight forwarder.

questions.question: What is an HS Code (Harmonized System Code)?
options: A standardized international code used to classify traded products for customs purposes
questions.answer: A standardized international code used to classify traded products for customs purposes
questions.explanation: The Harmonized System (HS) is an international nomenclature for classifying products. It allows participating countries to classify traded goods on a common basis. HS codes determine applicable tariff rates and trade statistics.

questions.question: Demurrage in shipping refers to:
options: Charges for exceeding the free time allowed to unload or return containers
questions.answer: Charges for exceeding the free time allowed to unload or return containers
questions.explanation: Demurrage is a charge for keeping containers at the terminal beyond the free detention period. Detention is charged when containers are kept outside the terminal (at importer's premises) beyond free time.

questions.question: ETA stands for:
questions.explanation: ETA (Estimated Time of Arrival) is the expected date and time a vessel or shipment will arrive at the destination. ETD (Estimated Time of Departure) is the expected departure time.

questions.question: A freight forwarder's primary role is to:
options: Arrange transportation on behalf of shippers, handling logistics and documentation
questions.answer: Arrange transportation on behalf of shippers, handling logistics and documentation
questions.explanation: A freight forwarder acts as an intermediary between shippers and transportation services. They arrange cargo transportation, prepare documentation, handle customs clearance, and often consolidate LCL shipments.

questions.question: If the consignee picks up the container on December 31, how much demurrage would be charged?
questions.explanation: ETA is December 22. Free time is 7 days, so free time ends December 29. December 30 and 31 = 2 days of demurrage. 2 days × USD 150/day = USD 300.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of the phone call in the audio?
options: To confirm a container booking and discuss shipping terms
To request a quotation for air freight
questions.answer: To confirm a container booking and discuss shipping terms
questions.explanation: The conversation is between a freight forwarder and a shipper confirming details of an FCL booking including vessel, ETD, and Incoterms.

questions.question:
You are a logistics officer at Mekong Trading Company. Write an email (80-120 words) to your freight forwarder requesting a booking for the following shipment:
- 1 x 20GP container
- Goods: Electronic components
- Origin: Ho Chi Minh City
- Destination: Singapore
- Requested ETD: Around December 1, 2024
- Incoterms: CIF Singapore
questions.answer: Sample answer: Dear [Forwarder Name], I hope this email finds you well. I would like to request a container booking for the following shipment: 1 x 20GP container of electronic components from Ho Chi Minh City to Singapore, with a requested ETD around December 1, 2024. The shipment will be on CIF Singapore terms. Please kindly advise on vessel availability, freight rates, and document requirements at your earliest convenience. Thank you for your assistance. Best regards, [Name]
questions.explanation: A good booking request email should include: type of container, commodity, origin/destination, requested ETD, Incoterms, and a polite request for available options.

questions.question: Explain the difference between FOB and CIF Incoterms in 3-4 sentences. Include when risk transfers in each case.
questions.answer: FOB means the seller delivers goods on board the vessel at the port of shipment. Risk transfers to the buyer when goods are on board. Under CIF, the seller pays for cost, insurance, and freight to the destination port, but risk still transfers when goods are loaded on board at the port of origin.
questions.explanation: Key points: FOB - seller responsibility ends at port of loading; CIF - seller pays freight and insurance to destination but risk transfers at same point as FOB.
